items_missed: Section 1 (Set Agenda): asked "do you have time to go over some details and then I can give you pricing" but never gave a rough time estimate (the '10-15 minutes' piece) or an explicit 'sound good?' — relied on the customer's 'that would be great' to carry it.

Section 2 (Probe): never confirmed a destination address, zip code, or destination floor/stairs (only referenced it in passing as 'a one-story home'); never asked about additional rooms (garage, storage unit, balcony), storage stops, additional stops, or the 'anything you're worried about with this move?' stressor question.

Section 5 (Estimate): walk distance/clearance was discussed during the probe but never tied back in as a reason for the time range, and no equivalents or analogy (school bus, etc.) were used to make the estimate concrete.

Section 6 (Save Your Ass): no real prep speech — the closest was a vague 'how well prepared you are when we get there' line with no consolidation examples (toys, drawers, wall photos) and no 'take a carload' tip, so this doesn't clear the bar.
Section 8 (Politeness): used Isabella's name once, in the opening line ('may I speak with Isabella?'), and never again for the rest of the 9.6-minute call.

Section 9 (Bonus): delivery had several rambly, hard-to-follow stretches (mixed-up numbers on the clock minimum, garbled inventory recap, 'how well we prayed you are prepared') that a cleaner, slower pace would fix.
top_strength: The pricing and differentiators section was flawless: hourly rate, full no-hidden-fees pitch, No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, and On-Time Guarantee were all covered clearly and in the right order, and she explicitly contrasted No Worries with competitors' "state mandated 60 cents per pound coverage." The booking close was just as strong — no deposit, reply-to-email confirmation, easy reschedule policy — and it landed: Isabella closed the call with "Oh! That's so perfect. Thank you so much."
coaching_note: Your pricing pitch and booking close are close to a model call — keep doing them exactly like this. Two fixes: use Isabella's name more than once, it disappears right after your opening line and repeating it is a fast, free way to build warmth. And actually run the Save Your Ass prep speech — you hinted at 'being prepared' but never gave her the concrete payoff (prep = shorter move = lower bill) or a consolidation/carload example, and this call was a good fit for it since she's self-packing. Also tighten your delivery; there were a few spots where numbers and details got jumbled and a slower pace would clean that up.
phone_presence_notes: Isabella ended the call visibly delighted ("I love it, I love it, thank you so much") and the rep's tone stayed warm and confident throughout, but dropping the customer's name after the opening line and some rambly phrasing keep it just short of a 5.
audio_review_reason: Transcript has heavy ASR garbling on the rep's side (inventory recap, clock minimum, 'how well we prayed you are prepared') — worth a quick audio spot-check to confirm whether the rambling is real delivery or transcription noise.
